program_overview.title: Python for Teens: Beginner to Advanced
program_overview.tagline: One language carries a teenager from a first print statement to games, web apps, automation and AI projects. This is that road, walked properly in 10 months.
program_overview.description:
Python is the language teenagers can grow with: simple enough that a working program exists by the end of class one, serious enough that it runs Instagram’s backend and most of modern AI. This live online course takes students aged 13 to 18 from zero to genuinely advanced, with every concept practiced through projects a teen actually wants to build and keep.

The first three months build real foundations: variables to functions, the core data structures, files and JSON, algorithms, and object-oriented programming taught with patience instead of jargon. The middle months turn skill into products: 2D games with Pygame that get shared online, desktop apps, automation scripts that do real chores, web scraping done politely, and a first taste of data analysis with pandas. The final months put Python on the web with Flask, databases, user accounts and a real deployment, then finish with machine learning fundamentals, AI-powered features built on modern AI APIs, and a capstone shipped like a real product.

The pace is honest: two live classes a week plus three to four hours of practice, and the syllabus fits ten months of that rhythm. Students who need longer take up to twelve months, the class adapts instead of rushing ahead. Learning is checked the honest way too: homework after every class, monthly assignments that mix new questions with earlier topics, and a final exam that decides the certificate. Real knowledge, real work, real projects, depth over dopamine. By the end, a student owns a portfolio of 30+ projects, a web app on a public URL, and the kind of understanding that makes the next step, whether AI, data science or competitive programming, feel natural.
what_makes_this_different: Projects teens choose to keep: games, bots, automations and apps they actually use, not textbook exercises
An honest 10-month arc with 2 months of margin built in: students who need more practice time take up to 12, nobody is rushed
Modern Python throughout: the latest Python 3, VS Code, pytest, pandas and real AI APIs, the same tools working developers use
Every submitted project comes back with written feedback, and recurring gaps are reopened in class instead of left behind
A deployed capstone: the course ends with an app on the public internet, not screenshots on a laptop
Small live batches capped at 10 students, with mini-batch and 1-on-1 options for closer attention
Real assessment: weekly homework, mixed-review assignments every month, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with focused revision and a free retest for students who fall short

course_guarantees.certificate: A certificate you earn by passing the final exam, with a free retest after revision if needed.
course_guarantees.free_demo: A free demo class before you enrol, so you can decide with no pressure.

faqs.question: What will my teen build in this Python course?
faqs.answer: More than 30 real projects across ten months: arcade games in Pygame published on itch.io, desktop apps like study timers and flashcards, automation scripts that organize files and track prices, an honest data analysis of a real dataset, a Flask web app with user accounts deployed to a public URL, and a final AI-powered capstone. Every project is built by the student and reviewed with written feedback.

faqs.question: How long does it take a teenager to learn Python properly?
faqs.answer: Most students reach a genuinely advanced level in 10 months at 2 live classes a week plus 3 to 4 hours of practice. The syllabus deliberately keeps 2 months of margin in hand: students who need more repetition take up to 12 months, with no rushing and no penalty. Progress is visible early, the first playable text game appears within the first month.

faqs.question: How is my teen assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Classwork runs inside every session, homework follows every class, and each month ends with an assignment that deliberately mixes new questions with earlier topics so knowledge compounds instead of fading. Every phase closes with a cumulative check, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions drawn from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns a focused revision plan and a free retest. We optimize for real knowledge and real depth, not a stream of feel-good badges.

faqs.question: Does my teen need maths or prior coding experience?
faqs.answer: No prior coding at all, and ordinary school maths is plenty. The course teaches logical thinking from scratch, and the maths that appears, coordinates in games, averages in data analysis, grows naturally out of projects rather than being a prerequisite. Teens who already know some Python simply move faster through the early months.

faqs.question: Is Python the right first language for a teenager?
faqs.answer: For most teens, yes. Python reads close to English, produces a working program in the first class, and then scales all the way up: it is the language of choice in AI, data science and automation, and one of the two languages accepted in most school-level computer science exams. Nothing learned here has to be unlearned later.

faqs.question: What software is needed, and is it free?
faqs.answer: Everything is free: Python itself, the VS Code editor, and open-source libraries like Pygame, Flask, pandas and scikit-learn. Any reasonably modern computer with a stable internet connection can run the full course. Where an AI service needs an account, it is set up together with a parent.

faqs.question: How is AI taught in this course?
faqs.answer: In two honest layers. First, machine learning fundamentals with scikit-learn, where students train real models and learn to evaluate them without fooling themselves. Second, modern AI APIs, where they build features like a study-buddy that answers questions over their own notes. The goal is a teen who builds with AI and understands its limits, not one who just chats with it.

faqs.question: Where does this lead after the course?
faqs.answer: Three natural roads: our AI and Machine Learning Masterclass for teens who caught the AI spark, the Data Structures and Algorithms course for competitive programming, or deeper web development from Flask into Django and React. The portfolio built here, games, a deployed app, an AI capstone, carries directly into school projects and college applications.

faqs.question: How much does the Python course cost?
faqs.answer: ₹1,499 per month for group classes, with 2 live classes weekly and at most 10 teens per batch. Mini batches of 3-4 students are ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International students pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.

faqs.question: Is a trial class available?
faqs.answer: Yes, a free demo class with no commitment; book at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. Parents are welcome to observe the demo and ask the teacher questions afterwards.

faqs.question: How are the classes taught?
faqs.answer: Through live 1-hour online sessions with a real teacher, never pre-recorded videos. Classes are interactive and small; students write and run code during class, not just watch someone else do it. Group batches are capped at 10, with mini-batch and 1-on-1 options for closer attention.

faqs.question: Does the course include a certificate?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is earned, not handed out: the certificate is awarded on passing the final exam, with a free retest after revision if the first attempt falls short. Alongside it stands the portfolio, 30+ projects, published games, a deployed web app and an AI capstone, which shows exactly what your teen can build, not just what they sat through.
